transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, doctor, it's... it's a bit hard to explain, but I suppose what really made me finally pick up the phone and come in today is that my eating has just gotten all turned around lately. I used to be so good about my schedule, you know, having my little meals at the proper times, setting the table for myself even if it's just me. But now, it's like my whole internal clock is broken. Some days I'll just be sitting in the living room, maybe looking out the window, and I'll glance over at the clock and it's suddenly past three or four in the afternoon, and I realize I completely forgot lunch. Just entirely slipped my mind, which isn't like me at all. 

And then, on the flip side of that, there are other days where I just can't seem to settle down. I'll wander into the kitchen and just stand right there at the counter—not even pulling out a chair to sit down properly—and I'll just start eating whatever is in front of me. Mostly crackers, or whatever sweets I have tucked away in the cupboards. I'll just stand there eating and eating. And the strangest part of it all is that nothing even tastes right anymore. I'll be chewing on a cookie or a cracker, and it's just... dull. Like chewing on cardboard. There's no real flavor to it, no joy in it at all, but I just keep standing there putting it in my mouth anyway. It's just all so out of sorts, and it's been bothering me so much because I just don't understand why my appetite is doing this...
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?

Well, yes, I suppose I have. It’s hard to put into words exactly, but it’s just this terrible heaviness. Most mornings, I wake up and before I’ve even thrown off the covers or put my feet on the floor, I just feel so low. It’s like... well, it’s like all the color has just drained right out of the day before I’ve even gotten dressed. I used to love the mornings, you know? I’d open the curtains, let the sun in, maybe listen to the birds for a bit while I put the kettle on. But now, it’s just this gray, heavy blanket over everything. I just lie there thinking, 'What’s the point of getting up?' And it’s not just a passing feeling, it lingers. I’ll finally get myself out of bed, but that heavy feeling just follows me around the house all day, from the bedroom to the kitchen to the living room. It’s exhausting, really, just feeling so... weighed down by it all. I keep hoping I’ll wake up and feel like my old self again, but it’s just been this same dreary feeling morning after morning.
Have you been having any recurring thoughts that you can't seem to get out of your head?

Well, yes, actually, now that you mention it... there is something that's been just going round and round in my mind, and I know it sounds odd, I really do. I've even hesitated to mention it to my daughter because she might think I'm just getting confused in my old age, but I'm not. You see, I have this old wooden filing cabinet in the spare bedroom—my late husband bought it at an estate sale back in 1982, beautiful oak thing—and that's where I keep all our important papers. Birth certificates, old hospital records, the deed to the house, all neatly organized in manila folders. 

But lately, when I go in there to check on things, I get this overwhelming feeling... no, I *know*... that certain dates and names in those family papers are being changed. Or hidden from me. I'll look at a hospital bill from years ago, and the dates just don't line up with what I remember, or a middle initial on a document will look slightly altered. It's like... like the hospital, or maybe even someone in the family, is slipping in there when I'm not looking and rearranging things. And it's not just to mess with my files, no, it feels like they are sending me little messages through the records. Like there's a code or a secret meaning in why that specific date was changed, or why that particular paper was moved to the back of the folder. I'll sit on the edge of the guest bed for hours, just staring at these papers, trying to decipher what they're trying to tell me. It's exhausting, really, because I can't stop thinking about it, even when I'm trying to watch my evening programs or make a cup of tea. I just keep wondering, what is the message? Why are they doing this to my papers?
Do you believe these changes to your papers are actually happening, or do you think it might be a mistake or your imagination?

Well, doctor, that's just the thing, isn't it? My daughter, when I finally did hint at it the other day while we were having our Sunday tea—she brought over those lovely lemon scones from the bakery down on Main Street—she said, "Oh, Mom, your eyes are just playing tricks on you, you need new reading glasses." But I know it's not my eyes. I've had the same prescription for three years, Dr. Henderson checked them himself just last November. No, it's not a mistake, and it's certainly not my imagination. 

I know it sounds odd to someone on the outside, I really do. If someone told me this ten years ago, I might have thought they were a bit touched. But when you're sitting there, holding a piece of paper you've looked at a dozen times over the last thirty years, and suddenly the date of my husband's knee surgery is off by two days, or the spelling of a doctor's name has an extra 'e' at the end... you just know. You feel it right down in your bones. It's real. 

And it's not just random mistakes, either. That's what convinces me it's not just a clerical error from decades ago that I'm only just now noticing. It's too specific. It's like... well, like I said, it feels deliberate. Like the hospital, or maybe even someone in my own family—though heaven knows why they'd go through all that trouble—is sneaking in and altering these family papers just to send me these little messages through the records. Why else would they change the date on the deed to the house, just slightly? It has to mean something. It’s a message, I’m sure of it. I just haven’t quite pieced together what it is they’re trying to tell me yet, but I know it's happening. I know it is.
Do you think anyone or anything is actually controlling or influencing these changes to your papers?

Well, like I was saying just a moment ago... I know it sounds so very odd to say it out loud again, but yes, absolutely. I keep feeling that certain dates and names in our family papers are being changed or purposely hidden from me by someone who is pulling the strings behind the scenes. It really does feel like the hospital administration, or maybe even someone in my own family who is working with them, is controlling the whole thing. 

I've thought long and hard about how they're managing it, sitting there in the evenings. You see, we’ve always kept a spare key under the heavy ceramic frog on the back porch—my late husband Arthur bought that frog at a garden center over in Shelbyville back in, oh, it must have been 1998, or maybe '99—and I think they found it and are using it. They must wait until I go out to the grocery store on Tuesday mornings. I always go on Tuesdays, you see, because that's when they mark down the canned goods and the bakery items, and I like to get there right when the doors open. And while I'm out, they just slip right in through the back door. 

They must be coordinating the whole thing just to send me these little messages through the records. Why else would someone go through all the trouble of sneaking into a 74-year-old woman's spare bedroom just to alter the middle initial on an old hospital discharge paper or hide a billing statement from 2004? It has to be them orchestrating it. I just... I can't quite figure out how they know exactly when I'm leaving the house, unless they're parked down the street watching my driveway. I mean, it's a quiet neighborhood, you'd think Mrs. Gable next door would notice a strange car or someone walking up my path, but she's half deaf and never leaves her sunroom anyway, bless her heart, so she's no help at all. So yes, doctor, someone is definitely controlling it. They are going out of their way to manipulate those papers and leave me these messages in the folders, I just know it.
Do you feel like these people altering your papers are trying to harm you in some way?

Harm? Oh, well... harm is such a strong word, isn't it? I mean, I don't think they're going to come in and, you know, hit me over the head with that ceramic frog on the porch or anything violent like that. I don't feel like my life is in physical danger. But it is... well, it's a terrible mental toll, doctor. It really, truly is. 

Because, like I keep saying—and I know I keep coming back to this, and I know it sounds odd to keep repeating it, but it's just so heavy on my mind—I just keep feeling that certain dates and names in our family papers are being changed or hidden from me. And when you're sitting there, day after day, trying to piece together why the hospital or someone in the family is sending me little messages through the records, it just wears you down to an absolute nub. 

Is it harm? Well, it certainly doesn't feel good. It makes my chest tight and my stomach all fluttery. I'll be sitting there in the evening, the television is on—I usually watch Wheel of Fortune, Pat Sajak is just so comforting, though I know he's retiring soon, which is a shame—and I can't even focus on the word puzzles. I can't even enjoy my evening because I'm just thinking about those folders in the oak cabinet. I'm sitting there thinking, what does the altered date mean? Why did they hide Arthur's billing statement? 

If they aren't trying to harm me, then why on earth are they being so incredibly secretive about it all? Why not just call me on the telephone? I have a perfectly good landline. It's one of those old cream-colored ones hanging on the kitchen wall, with the long cord. I've never gotten rid of it because it always works, even during the spring thunderstorms when the power goes out. They could just pick up the phone and call me if they had something to say. But no, they have to sneak around my house while I'm at the grocery store and alter my personal records to send me these messages. So maybe they aren't trying to physically hurt me, but they're certainly trying to drive me to distraction. They are turning my own home, my own safe place, into some kind of puzzle that I have to solve, and it's just exhausting.
Do you believe these messages you think are being sent to you through the altered papers are specifically about you or your life?

Well, yes, of course they are. I mean... whose else would they be about? I know I must sound like a broken record today, and I know it sounds odd to keep bringing it up, but I just keep feeling that certain dates and names in our family papers are being changed or hidden from me. And the thing is, they are *my* family papers. It’s exactly like I was saying before—it feels like the hospital, or maybe someone in the family, is sending me these little messages through the records, and they are using my own life story to do it.

Why else would they pick my house? It’s not like they’re sneaking into Mrs. Gable’s sunroom next door to change her old tax returns or her utility bills. No, it’s my husband Arthur’s discharge papers. It’s the deed to the house we bought together back in 1972. I keep all of these things in the bottom drawer of the heavy oak filing cabinet in the spare bedroom, the one with the brass handles that always stick a little bit when it's humid out. They are going into *my* cabinet, looking at *my* life, and altering the names and the dates that belong to me. 

So yes, it has to be about me. It’s so deeply personal. It feels like they are trying to tell me something specific about my past, or maybe something I missed, or something I’m supposed to do now that I'm on my own. I’ll sit there in the armchair with my cup of decaf Earl Grey tea—I simply can't drink regular tea after three o'clock or I'll be up all night staring at the ceiling fan, my system just can't handle the caffeine anymore—and I just look at these altered documents, trying to decipher what my role in all this puzzle is. Because it has to be about me, doctor. It’s my life they’re editing. I just haven't figured out exactly what the message about my life is supposed to mean yet, but they wouldn't go through all this trouble if it weren't specifically meant for my eyes.
Do you think these messages you believe are being sent to you could be a product of your own mind?

My own mind? Oh, well... I suppose I understand why you might ask a thing like that. My niece, Susan—she lives over in Grand Rapids now, she moved there when her husband got a job at the furniture factory back in, oh, 2012 I think it was, or maybe late 2011—she says something similar when I try to talk to her about it. She says, "Auntie, you're just getting older, maybe your eyes are playing tricks on you, maybe you're just misremembering." But my mind is as sharp as a tack, doctor, it really is. I still do the Sunday crossword puzzle in pen, the big one in the local paper, and I rarely ever have to scratch a word out. I remember everyone's birthdays, I balance my own checkbook down to the penny every single month... 

So when you ask if I'm just making it all up in my head... no. No, I really don't think I am. I know I keep coming back to this same point, and believe me, I know exactly how odd it sounds when I say it out loud to you, but I just keep feeling that certain dates and names in our family papers are being changed or hidden from me. It's not just my imagination or my memory failing. I put my reading glasses on—the good ones with the little tortoiseshell frames I got from Dr. Lin over at the vision center by the mall—and I look right at the page, and I can see that things are different than they were. 

It's exactly like I was saying before, it feels so entirely real, like the hospital or someone in the family is purposefully sending me these little messages through the records. If it were just my own mind making things up, why on earth would I invent something so incredibly tedious? Why would my brain decide to change a single date on a billing statement from a decade ago or hide a specific middle initial on Arthur's old paperwork? I’ve always been such a practical woman. When the hot water heater broke in the dead of winter back in '94, I didn't sit around imagining things, I called the plumber and boiled water on the stove to wash the dishes. I deal with what is right in front of me. 

So no, I really don't believe it's just my mind playing tricks or inventing a story. The papers are changing. Someone is doing this, leaving those messages for me to find, even if I haven't quite caught them in the act yet. It's just too specific to be a product of my own imagination.
How long have you been noticing these changes in your papers?

How long? Well, let me sit and think on that for just a moment... 

Because it certainly hasn't been forever. Arthur and I, we always kept everything so meticulously organized, and I never had a single reason to second-guess a piece of mail or a medical record. But these... well, the ideas about hidden messages in the family and medical papers started about a year and a month ago. 

I know the timing so precisely because it was right around the time the compressor on my deep freezer went out in the garage. I had a whole quarter of a cow in there from the local butcher, plus all my frozen strawberry preserves from the summer before, and I was in an absolute panic trying to save it all before it thawed and ruined the garage floor. That was exactly a year and a month ago. I had gone into the spare room, to that heavy oak cabinet I told you about, to find the original warranty for the freezer—I bought it at Sears back when they still had that lovely appliance department at the mall, before everything closed down—and when I pulled out the family and medical files to get to the appliance receipts... well, that's when it all started. 

That was the very first time I looked down at the paperwork and realized the dates didn't line up, and the names had been tampered with. I remember just standing there with the folder in my hands, completely forgetting about the melting meat in the garage, just staring at this message someone had left for me in the margins of Arthur's old hospital bill. 

So it's been thirteen months of this. A year and a month of just... trying to figure out what these messages are supposed to mean, day in and day out. It feels like so much longer, to be perfectly honest with you, because when you spend every single evening worrying about your own files being edited behind your back, time just drags on so slowly. But yes, a year and a month since I first noticed what they were doing.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'messages' in the papers, and how you think they are related to each other?

Well, it’s… it’s a bit hard to explain, I suppose, because they’re all connected, but the connections don’t always make sense to other people. Like, I’ll be sitting there, looking through the papers, and I’ll try to explain it to Susan—my niece, you remember I mentioned her—or even just trying to explain it to myself, really. I’ll start by pointing out something on my sister’s old medicine list, the one from when she had that terrible bout of bronchitis back in ’98, and how a dosage number was changed. And then, before I know it, I’m suddenly talking about our grandmother’s birth certificate, which I keep in the very back of the third folder, and how the county clerk’s signature looks like it was tracing over a different name entirely. 

And they are related, they really are, because it’s all part of the same family history, the same… the same story they’re trying to tell me. But when I try to lay it all out, to explain the appointments or the genealogy notes and how one thing leads to another, people just look at me blankly. Susan will say, "Auntie, I can’t follow what you mean, you’re jumping all over the place." And I suppose I am, because there’s just so much of it, so many little details that have been altered. It’s like a web, you see? You pull on one string, like a hospital bill, and it vibrates all the way over to a deed from fifty years ago. I try to explain how the dates on Arthur’s discharge match up with the missing middle initials on the tax forms, but my words just… they get all tangled up in the sheer volume of it all, and people tell me they just can't keep up with what I'm saying.
Can you describe one of these messages you've found in the papers, from start to finish, without leaving out any details?

From start to finish? Oh, my. Well... I don't know if I can actually do that. I know you want me to just pull one out and lay it flat on the table, so to speak, but... I'm really not sure I can separate just one out like that. 

You see, it’s not like reading a regular letter in the mail, where someone says 'Dear Auntie' at the top and signs 'Love, Susan' at the bottom. If it were like that, I could recite it to you right now. I have a wonderful memory for things like that. I can still recite the poem I learned for the spring recital in the eleventh grade—it was a lovely piece by Robert Frost, and I wore a yellow dress my mother made on her old Singer sewing machine. But these messages in the papers, they just don't work that way. 

I try, I really do. I’ll sit down at the dining room table—I always put a vinyl tablecloth down first, the one with the little sunflowers on it, so I don’t scratch the wood, because Arthur was so particular about that table—and I’ll open up the folders. I’ll say to myself, 'Alright, I am going to trace just this one thing so I can explain it properly.' But the moment I start looking at, say, a billing statement, and I see how the date has been nudged forward by three days, my eyes go right to the account number. And that number links to the zip code on a piece of medical mail from years ago, and before I know it, the beginning of the message is completely gone and I'm looking at something else entirely. 

It’s all just fragments, doctor. Little pieces scattered across decades of paperwork. So to give you one single message, from start to finish, without leaving anything out... I just can't do it. There really isn't a clear start or a finish to any of them, it’s just a constant... shifting of the ink all over the place. I wish I could give you a better answer, I really do, because I want you to understand what I'm going through, but I just don't have one neat little message to hand over to you.
Do you think it's possible that your interpretation of these changes in the papers might be mistaken, even if the changes themselves are real?

Mistaken? Well... I suppose anyone can be mistaken about anything, can't they? I mean, I’m not so stubborn that I can’t admit when I’ve made a simple error. Just last week, for instance, I was absolutely certain I had bought a tin of evaporated milk for my tea—I always use evaporated milk, never fresh, because it lasts so much longer in the cupboard and Arthur got me into the habit of it decades ago—but when I checked the pantry shelf, it just wasn't there. So I know I can be wrong about everyday things. 

And I know... well, I know it sounds odd. I really do know how it sounds when I say it out loud to you in a doctor's office. I'm not a foolish woman. But when it comes to these papers... I just can't shake it. I keep feeling that certain dates and names in our family papers are being changed or hidden from me on purpose. It's not just a typo here or a smudge there, which is what I tried to tell myself at first. 

I’ll sit there with my reading glasses on—the ones with the little rhinestones on the corners that Susan bought me for my seventieth birthday, because she said I needed something a little more stylish—and I’ll stare at a date on a discharge summary, and I’ll tell myself, 'Now, you’re just misinterpreting this, it's just a clerical error.' But then I see the name next to it, and the middle initial is suddenly missing, or a letter is swapped, and that feeling just washes right back over me. It feels so deliberate, like the hospital, or maybe even someone in the family, is sending me little messages through the records. 

It’s like they know I’m the only one who keeps these old files, the only one who takes the time to look through them, so they’re hiding these things right there in plain sight for me to find. So, even though I try my hardest to tell myself I might just be mistaken, the feeling that they are changing these things to communicate with me... it's just too strong to ignore. I keep going back to it. I just wish I knew exactly what the hospital or whoever it is actually wants me to do with the information, because it's terribly exhausting trying to piece it all together on my own.
Was there something significant happening in your life around the time you first noticed these changes in your papers, about a year and a month ago?

A year and a month? Well, no, doctor, actually... if we're being precise—and I do try to be very precise about these things, especially since the dates are so important—it’s been a bit longer than that. This whole change, the things happening with the papers, it's actually been going on for about a year and five months now. 

I know exactly when it started because you asked if something significant was happening, and... well, yes, there certainly was. That was right when my sister’s health took that serious turn. You see, she had always been the robust one in our family. Even when we were little girls in grade school, she was the one who never caught the winter colds, while I was always stuck in bed with the sniffles and a thermometer in my mouth. But then, about a year and five months ago—it was right at the end of the summer, I remember clearly because the terrible August heat had finally broken and I was just getting ready to take my lighter dresses down to the dry cleaners on Elm Street—she had this awful, sudden decline. 

We had to rush her to the hospital, and it was just a dreadful time. There was so much waiting around in those cold, sterile hallways, drinking that awful bitter coffee from the vending machine while the doctors ran test after test. It was terribly frightening, it really was, seeing her look so frail and small in that hospital bed when she'd always been so strong. 

And because I was so worried, I thought to myself, 'Well, I need to get her medical history in perfect order.' I felt like I needed to make sure the doctors had absolutely everything they could possibly need to figure out what was wrong with her. So I went home and I got all the family folders out, and I spread them all across the dining room table. I was sitting there late into the night, just poring over every single document, every old prescription and discharge note, trying to be helpful. And that’s exactly when it started. That’s when I first noticed the dates didn't look right, and the initials were moving around. So it hasn't been a year and a month, it's been exactly a year and five months, starting right when everything with my sister went so terribly wrong.
Do you still believe that someone is altering your papers to send you messages?

Well, yes, doctor. I do. Like I was just saying a few minutes ago, I know it sounds odd—I really am fully aware of how strange it must sound to a professional like yourself, and I don't blame you for asking again to make sure you understood me correctly. But I do still believe it, because it simply hasn't stopped. I still keep feeling that certain dates and names in our family papers are being changed or hidden from me on purpose. 

Just this morning, for instance, right before I put my good wool coat on to come down here to see you—the navy blue one, because there was quite a chill in the air today and my joints ache if I don't bundle up—I took one last look at a stack of Medicare summaries I had left out on the credenza in the hallway. I wasn't even going to look at them, I was just looking for my house keys, but my eye caught the top page. And sure enough, a middle initial that was clear as day on Tuesday was just... gone. Obscured. Hidden completely. 

So yes, even though I try to rationalize it and tell myself I'm just an old woman with too much time on her hands, I still feel exactly like the hospital, or perhaps someone in the family who knows I check these things, is sending me little messages through the records. It’s an ongoing thing, doctor, it didn't just happen once and go away. The papers keep changing. I just wish they would come out and tell me what they want to say plainly, instead of all this hiding and shifting of the ink, because it takes up so much of my day just trying to keep track of it all.
Do you still think the changes in your papers are real, even if no one else can see them?

Well, yes, doctor. I know we keep going over this, and I know I’ve said it a few times already today, but yes, I absolutely do believe they are real. 

I actually tried showing my daughter, Susan, just last Sunday. She came over for a roast—I always do a small beef roast on Sundays, even if it’s just the two of us now, with carrots and those little red potatoes she’s liked since she was a little girl in pigtails—and after dinner, I brought out one of the folders. I pointed right to a discharge paper from 2018, right where the ink was different, where the name was clearly altered. And she just sighed, you know how daughters sigh, that heavy sort of exhale, and told me it looked perfectly normal to her. She said it was just a smudge from the hospital's printer and that I was working myself up over nothing. 

But I know what I see, doctor. I know it sounds terribly odd to keep harping on it, and I know Susan thinks I'm just being a fussy old woman, but I keep feeling that certain dates and names in our family papers are being changed or hidden from me. It’s not a printer smudge. It’s just too specific. Even if Susan can't see it, or perhaps just doesn't *want* to see it because it makes her uncomfortable, I know the hospital, or maybe someone else in the family who knows I'm the keeper of the records, is sending me these little messages. 

Maybe they use a special ink that shifts over time, or maybe it's because I'm the only one who looks at them in the proper light. I have that nice brass reading lamp in the study, the one with the green glass shade that belonged to my late husband, and when you hold the paper just so under that light, you can see where the letters used to be and how they've been moved around. So yes, to answer your question, I do think they are real. It's just awfully frustrating when you can see something as plain as day, and the person sitting right across from you eating your roast beef tells you it's not there. It makes you feel like you're speaking a completely different language, it really does.
Do you feel like you have any control over these changes that are being made to your papers?

Control? Oh, heavens no, doctor. None at all. And that is perhaps the most distressing part of this whole ordeal. If I had any control over it, I would have put a stop to it months ago, I assure you. 

I've actually tried to stop it, you know. Just last month, I was getting so terribly overwhelmed by it all that I walked down to the hardware store—the one on Main Street, Mr. Henderson's old place, though his son runs it now—and I bought myself a heavy metal lockbox. One of those sturdy gray ones with a little silver key. I thought to myself, 'Well, if I lock the folders away where nobody can get to them, then the letters will have to stay put.' I took all the most important documents, the ones I knew had been tampered with, and I placed them inside. I even put the little silver key on a velvet ribbon and wore it around my neck, tucked right under my blouse, even when I was sleeping. I thought I had finally outsmarted whoever was doing this.

But it didn't make a lick of difference. When I opened the box three days later to check a billing statement... well, there it was again. The ink had shifted. 

Like I've been explaining to you, and I know I keep repeating myself and I know it sounds so very odd to keep saying it, but I just keep feeling that certain dates and names in our family papers are being changed or hidden from me, no matter what I do to protect them. It's exactly like the hospital, or perhaps someone in our own family, is determined to send me these little messages through the records, and they somehow find a way to alter the pages even when they are locked tight in a metal box. 

So no, I don't have any control over it whatsoever. It just happens, right under my nose, despite my best efforts to keep everything secure. I'm just left sitting there at my dining room table, trying to decipher what on earth they're trying to tell me this time. It’s exhausting, doctor, it truly is, having to constantly be on guard when you don't even have the power to stop it from happening.
Do you think it's possible that your belief in these changes is a product of your own anxiety or stress, rather than actual alterations to the papers?

Well... I suppose anyone in my shoes would be a little stressed, doctor. I mean, my goodness, just keeping up with the property taxes and the price of groceries these days is enough to give anyone a touch of anxiety. And my daughter Susan is always telling me I worry too much about keeping the house up since my husband passed away. So yes, I do have stress in my life, just like any normal person my age. 

But is it just my mind playing tricks on me because I'm anxious? No. No, I really don't think so. I know what anxiety feels like, you see. I get a little flutter in my chest when I have to drive on the interstate, or when the telephone rings too late at night and you worry it's bad news. That's what stress feels like to me. This... this situation with the papers is completely different. 

If it were just stress, wouldn't I be imagining things everywhere? Wouldn't I think the grocery receipts were changing, or the television Guide? But it's only the important documents. The medical records, the billing statements. Why would my anxiety be so terribly specific? 

I know I sound like a broken record today, and I know it sounds odd to keep bringing it back to this, but I just keep feeling that certain dates and names in our family papers are being changed or hidden from me. It’s not a feeling of panic, it’s a feeling of being communicated with, in this terribly roundabout way. It feels exactly like the hospital, or someone in the family who has access to these things, is sending me little messages through the records. 

It just doesn't make sense to me that everyday stress would cause ink to disappear or shift around on the page, especially when I've locked them away in that metal box I told you about. So, while I appreciate that you have to ask these things—it is your job, after all, and you're being very thorough, which I do appreciate in a doctor—I just can't agree that it's all in my head. The changes are there, clear as a bell. I just wish I knew what they were trying to say so I could finally put the whole matter to rest and get back to my normal routine.
